To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we present a novel approach for the simulation of a biventricular FE model coupled to a lumped-circuit model; (2) the model was validated by comparing the model output to experimental data; (3) the model was used to study the effects of dilated cardiomyopathic changes in the heart; and (4) the model was shown to be computationally efficient.
the developed model is able to simulate cardiac function and myofibre stress for both healthy and diseased hearts.

we have developed a new computational approach that can be used to model the heart and circulatory system in a weakly coupled manner and that the approach has been validated by comparing its results to experimental measurements and to the results of a fully coupled model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to modelling the cardiovascular system that combines the advantages of FE models and lumped-parameter models.
the development of a numerical tool for the simulation of cardiac function and its application to the investigation of the effect of heart failure on the heart.
the development of a computational model that can be used to simulate the effects of various treatment strategies in heart failure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented model is a promising tool for investigating the effects of heart diseases and their treatments.
the proposed method provides a useful tool for studying the interaction of the heart with the circulatory system in a computationally efficient manner.
the presented method is an important step forward in the development of an accurate and efficient model for the simulation of the cardiovascular system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a novel, efficient approach for modelling the heart and circulatory system interaction.

we have successfully coupled a finite element model of the heart to a lumped parameter model of the circulatory system and have shown the ability of the model to simulate the effects of cardiomyopathy.
the coupling approach presented here provides a good balance between the level of detail and computation time required for simulating the cardiovascular system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the weak coupling approach can be used to simulate the effects of heart disease on the cardiovascular system, with the advantage of being computationally efficient.

we have demonstrated that a weakly coupled FE model can be used to study the interaction between the ventricles and the circulatory systems, which is an essential step towards the development of a fully coupled FE model.
we have developed a fast, yet accurate, computational tool that can be used to assess the effects of heart disease and to test the effectiveness of potential treatments.
